penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A checkpointing middleware or proxy layer for AI agent platforms requires per-platform custom integration and debugging work that cannot be automated away — maintaining compatibility with Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor APIs as they change requires ongoing manual engineering effort.

rationale: The buyers are individual paid subscribers to AI platforms — mostly freelancers and developers paying personal subscription fees, not business budget lines — which makes monetization as an additional paid tool unlikely at meaningful price points. The core technical challenge (checkpointing agent state across opaque third-party APIs) is deeply non-trivial: each platform (Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor) exposes different internals, and maintaining a working proxy layer would require constant engineering re-work as those APIs evolve, far exceeding what a solo non-technical operator can sustain. Willingness to pay for a workaround tool when the real fix is the upstream platform's responsibility is also questionable. Drop and monitor in case a platform opens state-checkpointing APIs.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. The problem is real but the solution requires low-level integration with multiple closed AI platform APIs that change frequently, making it impossible for a solo non-technical operator to build and maintain without a dedicated engineering team. The buyer (individual platform subscriber) is also unlikely to pay a meaningful monthly fee for a workaround that the underlying platform should fix for free. A simpler adjacent product — a quota-burn monitoring dashboard that shows token usage vs. task completion — is more buildable but still faces a weak buyer-clarity problem. Recommend dropping and revisiting if any major AI platform publishes agent-state APIs.
notes: operational_autonomy (3) and buildability_with_ai (4) both fail build gates. Buyer clarity (5) also fails the build gate floor of 6. Total of 3.2 is below the validate threshold of 5.5.
